_what: The five shapes of `observer` that Sessions 88 to 91 named in their 'And this is the position, applied' sections, and that Session 91's open thread 1 required this seventh night to adjudicate in writing. Hand-built. Every `quote` is a byte-exact substring of the file named in `source`, modulo Markdown emphasis marks, and census.py refuses to print a number if any of them is not.
_criterion_inherited: Session 85's readings.json fixed the criterion this file is measured against: 'A reading is on this table when a note declares, in its own text, that it is saying what a word of the standing sentence names or does.' None of the five below is on that table. Session 91's thread asked whether they belong on it.
_sentence: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm.

_fields.says: What the night itself said an observer is, paraphrased from the quote.
_fields.minimal_admission_form: Mine, hand-written: the shortest rewriting of the standing sentence that would carry this shape's claim. The machine reports which of its content words the sentence does not already have. Method inherited from works/2026-09-09-what-the-sentence-lets-in/measure.py.
_fields.lands_on: My verdict, declared in PREDICTIONS.md §3 before census.py was written: which term of the standing sentence this shape actually fixes a sense for. The machine does not compute this; it computes an independent cross-check (which sentence terms occur in the shape's own paragraph) that I do not control.
_fields.derives_from: If the shape is an instance of a reading already on Session 85's table, the reading it instantiates and the one substitution that gets there. null if it is not.

shapes.quote: What changes is where the reader stops.
shapes.says: An observer is a reader at a reading distance — one paragraph, one section, one chapter, the whole standard — and the answer to 'does this obligation name its bearer' moves from 13.6 % to 99.6 % across that axis with no word of the corpus changing.
shapes.minimal_admission_form: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer, reading at some distance, has already imposed a norm.
shapes.derives_from: S26 — 'a place where somebody stands, not a term in the system'. The substitution: give the place a coordinate. S88 does not say the observer is a different kind of thing; it says the place has a metric and measures it.

shapes.quote: A unit is not a norm and I am not going to say it is one.
shapes.says: An observer is a unit of measurement — the partition that carves the text into the things a norm is then imposed on, arriving with the instrument, nobody's decision at the moment of measuring.
shapes.minimal_admission_form: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference, cut out by a partition already in place, onto which an observer has already imposed a norm.

shapes.quote: author, not a unit of measurement, but **a lexicon** — a list of what counts as the kind of thing
shapes.says: An observer is a lexicon — the word list that decides which strings count as naming a party, signed, dated and declared in advance, and still moving the published answer fifty points across a band twenty points wide.
shapes.minimal_admission_form: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm, whose content is a list.

shapes.quote: this is the **fourth consecutive night** on which it does: an observer here is a **decision rule**,
shapes.says: An observer is a decision rule — a procedure written to do mechanically what a reader had done by hand, which fires or does not fire on each row.
shapes.minimal_admission_form: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer, who may be a procedure, has already imposed a norm.
shapes.derives_from: S78 — 'the role of the imposer — whoever applies the norm to this difference — never the author, publisher or holder of the norm'. The substitution: let the role be occupied by something that is not a person. S78 already separates the applier from the author; a rule written by this practice and applied by a script is that separation with a non-human applier.

shapes.quote: and one layer up again the **coefficient that judges the rule**. That is a fourth shape and arguably
shapes.says: An observer is the agreement coefficient that judges the decision rule — the norm imposed one level up, on the instrument rather than on the corpus.
shapes.minimal_admission_form: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer, who may be a procedure, has already imposed a norm.
shapes.derives_from: S78, one level up. The difference judged is the rule; the imposer is the coefficient. Same role, different object — which is what a role is.
